email.subject: Your parcel is waiting!!! pay small fee

body.v: Your parcle is held at our depot. You must pay a small fee of CHF 2.50 today or it will be send back.

hotspots.explain: A free-looking mailbox address, not parcelpoint.example. A real parcel company writes from its own domain.
"Dear costumer" is generic and misspelt. Your real parcel company knows your name.
"Today or it will be sent back" is there to rush you.
A strange address on a different domain that has nothing to do with ParcelPoint.
More spelling mistakes. Companies proofread; scammers often do not.

who.prompt: Who is really writing to you? Look at the address, not just the name.
who.answer: Not ParcelPoint. The address is on free-mailbox.example, not parcelpoint.example, and the spelling mistakes are not how a real parcel company writes.
choices: Someone using a throwaway mailbox, not ParcelPoint

emotion.prompt: What feeling is this email trying to create?
emotion.answer: Hurry: pay today or lose the parcel.
choices: Hurry: pay today or the parcel goes back
None: it is a plain notice

ask.prompt: What exactly does it want you to do?
ask.answer: Pay a fee through a link, which would hand your card details to the sender.
choices: Collect the parcel from a neighbour
Pay a fee through a link

verify.prompt: How can you check through a channel you control?
verify.answer: Ignore the link. Open the ParcelPoint app, or type the address yourself, and look up your parcels.
choices: Pay the small fee, just in case
Look up your parcels in the ParcelPoint app, opened yourself
Reply and ask for a different link

actions.label: Open the ParcelPoint app yourself and check your parcels
actions.consequence: No parcel is on hold. The email was fake and you gave nothing away.

actions.label: Pay the fee through the link
actions.consequence: Your card details go to the scammer, who can spend your money.

actions.label: Report the email as phishing and delete it
actions.consequence: Good call. Nothing was clicked and your mail provider learns to catch the next one.

attacker_reveal: Spelling mistakes, a stranger's address and a fee small enough that nobody checks... I did not even try. This still catches people who are waiting for a parcel.
